" It was on account of thy prostration and the exhaustion of 
thy steeds and in order to mitigate this terrible fatigue, that I 
undertook those specific measures. It was not from caprice, 0 
Warrior, that I drove the chariot away; it was devotion to my

thou desires!, 0 Hero, 0 Scourge of Thy Foes, and I shall 
fulfil it implicidy with all my heart ! " 
Then Ravana, fully satisfied with the reply of his charioteer, 
addressed many words of praise to him and, in his martial atdour, 
said:-
" Speedily drive my chariot towards Ragbava, 0 Charioteer, 
Ravana is incapable of turning back ere he bas destroyed his 
enemies in battle ! " 
Speaking thus, the King of the Titans standing in his chariot, 
bestowed a brilliant ring of great price on his charioteer and, 
under his orders, the driver set out to the banlefield. Urged on 
by Ravana's command, the charioteer whipped his steeds into 
a gallop and, in an instant, the great chariot belonging to that 
Indra among the Titans stood before Rama in the field.

brief.summary_1line: As Rama stands exhausted before Ravana, the sage Agastya teaches him the Aditya Hridaya hymn to the Sun to restore strength and assure victory.

image_candidates.scene_text: The sage Agastya appears on the battlefield before the weary Rama and instructs him in the radiant Hymn to the Sun as Ravana waits in his chariot.
Rama stands in the war-torn field with folded hands, reciting the Aditya Hridaya while the blazing sun shines above him.
Ravana’s massive chariot drawn by galloping steeds rushes toward Rama as the final duel looms.

deep.rich_summary: As the climactic battle between Rama and Ravana resumes, Ravana orders his charioteer to drive him straight back into combat, refusing to retreat until his enemy is destroyed. Meanwhile Rama stands momentarily exhausted on the battlefield. At this critical moment the sage Agastya appears among the assembled gods and reveals a sacred teaching: the Aditya Hridaya, a hymn to the Sun. Agastya explains that the Sun is the cosmic source of creation, time, energy, and victory, honored by gods and demons alike. Reciting this eternal hymn dispels fear, grants strength, and ensures triumph in peril. Rama meditates on the Sun, chants the hymn, purifies himself, and regains courage and clarity, preparing to confront Ravana again. The episode frames the coming victory as both martial and cosmic, aligning Rama with divine order and solar power.

highlight_spans.why: Opening discussion of charioteer strategy sets the tactical stage for the impending decisive clash.
Agastya approaches Rama and introduces the secret hymn that will enable him to defeat all adversaries.
Part of the grand hymn praising the Sun as creator, sustainer, and cosmic force worshipped by gods and demons.
Agastya promises victory to the one who recites the hymn, directly foreshadowing Rama's triumph over Ravana.
Rama's grief lifts as he meditates on the Sun and regains strength before resuming the battle.

top_scenes.scene_text: The sage Agastya appears radiant among gathered gods on the battlefield and instructs the weary Rama while Ravana waits in his towering war chariot.
Rama stands in the war-torn field at dawn, hands folded toward the blazing Sun as he recites the Aditya Hridaya while armies pause around him.
Ravana's massive chariot thunders forward across the battlefield, the demon king crowned and furious as he charges toward Rama.
